prompt: # Game Development Brief: "Sky Runner - Aviation Endless Runner"## Core ConceptBuild a 3D endless runner game inspired by Subway Surfers but with a CUSTOM AIRPLANE/THEME. Instead of running on train tracks, the player pilots a small aircraft through an aerial obstacle course.## Key Differences from Subway Surfers| Subway Surfers | Sky Runner (This Game) ||---------------|------------------------|| Ground-based running | Aerial flight mechanics || Train tracks | Sky lanes with cloud corridors || Jump/roll/dodge | Pitch up/down, barrel roll, boost || Coin collection | Fuel orbs + cargo packages || Police chase | Storm cloud pursuit system |## Game Mechanics1. **Movement:** 3-lane horizontal system (left, center, right) + vertical pitch control2. **Actions:** - Swipe Up: Climb altitude - Swipe Down: Dive - Swipe Left/Right: Change lanes - Double Tap: Barrel roll (invincibility frame)3. **Obstacles:** - Other aircraft (must dodge) - Storm clouds (slowdown zone) - Bird flocks (damage) - Air traffic control towers - Turbulence zones4. **Collectibles:** - Fuel orbs (extend run time) - Cargo crates (bonus points) - Golden propellers (currency) - Power-ups: Turbo boost, Shield, Magnet## Visual Style- **Art Direction:** Low-poly stylized 3D (like Subway Surfers but aviation-themed)- **Color Palette:** Sky blues, sunset oranges, cloud whites, metallic grays- **Environment:** Dynamic skybox with day/night cycle, volumetric clouds- **Player Character:** Customizable pilot with different aircraft skins- **UI:** Minimalist HUD, altitude meter, fuel gauge, score counter## Technical Stack- **Engine:** Unity 2023 LTS or Three.js (for web-based)- **Language:** C# (Unity) or JavaScript/TypeScript (Three.js)- **Physics:** Custom arcade physics (not realistic flight sim)- **Platform:** Mobile (iOS/Android) + Web GL- **Performance:** 60 FPS target, LOD system for distant objects## Required Features1. **Main Menu:** Hangar scene with aircraft selection2. **Game Loop:** Endless procedurally generated sky lanes3. **Progression:** Unlock new planes, pilots, and trails4. **Leaderboard:** Global and friend scores5. **Daily Challenges:** Specific mission types (collect X fuel, dodge Y birds)6. **Shop System:** In-game currency for cosmetics7. **Save System:** Cloud save for progress## Deliverables- Complete project structure- Player controller script with swipe gestures- Obstacle spawning system (object pooling)- Collision detection and damage system- UI manager (score, fuel, game over screen)- 3 sample aircraft models (placeholder or procedurally generated)- Background music + SFX placeholders## Unique Selling Points1. **Verticality:** Unlike Subway Surfers, players can change altitude2. **Aircraft Customization:** Wings, engines, paint jobs, contrail effects3. **Weather System:** Dynamic weather affects gameplay (rain = slippery, wind = lane drift)4. **Multiplayer Mode:** Real-time race against ghost data of other players# OutputGenerate the complete codebase structure, core gameplay scripts, and UI components. Include comments for easy customization. Make it modular for future feature additions.

Role: Act as an expert Android App Developer specialized in low-latency screen mirroring and remote input protocols.​Task: Create a dual-app system (one for Android Mobile and one for Android TV) that functions like a high-performance Remote Desktop.​Core Architecture:​Processing Distribution: The Mobile device must handle 90-95% of all computational tasks (CPU/GPU). The Android TV app should act as a 'Thin Client,' using only 4-5% of its processor to decode the video stream and relay input commands.​Connection: The devices will connect via the Mobile's Personal Hotspot and TV's Wi-Fi. Use a high-speed local socket connection (TCP/UDP) for data transfer.​Functionality:​Full Display Sharing: Stream the entire mobile UI to the TV in high definition with minimal latency.​Reverse Control: Any command given via the TV (using a TV remote, mouse, or keyboard connected to the TV) must be sent back to the mobile app. The mobile app will then execute these commands on the mobile's processor using 'Accessibility Services' or 'Root' (if available).​Screen Management: Include a feature where the mobile screen can be turned OFF while the processor remains active and continues to stream the display to the TV to save battery.​Optimization: Use H.264/H.265 hardware encoding on the mobile and hardware decoding on the TV for maximum speed.​User Interface: Simple 'Connect' button on both apps. Show a status indicator for CPU usage on both devices.​Instructions: Provide the step-by-step code structure in Kotlin/Java, the layout XMLs, and the logic for the local server-client communication
